title: Addition transport for supplied compatible comparisons
statement: Let U and V be schemes [def-pc-scheme], f : U → V, O a commutative ring sheaf on V’s small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and G an O-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let L be set inverse image, La the fixed abelian inverse image, and Lr any left adjoint to the sectionwise ring direct image. Assume L preserves finite limits and er : Lr ⋙ FrU ≅ FrV ⋙ L and ea : La ⋙ FaU ≅ FaV ⋙ L satisfy the hom-equivalence compatibility equations of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures]. Write X=FrV(O), Y=FaV(FV(G)), X'=FrU(Lr(O)), Y'=FaU(La(FV(G))), with Fr and Fa the underlying-set functors and FV the underlying abelian sheaf. For each site let e(P,Q) be the canonical categorical-product-to-sectionwise-product isomorphism. There exist addition morphisms axV : X⊗X→X, ayV : Y⊗Y→Y, ax : X'⊗X'→X', ay : Y'⊗Y'→Y', whose section values on pairs are the ordinary sums. Set cx=eU(X',X')⁻¹ ≫ prod.map(erO,erO) ≫ (prodComparison L X X)⁻¹ ≫ L(eV(X,X)), and define cy similarly using ea and Y. Then cx ≫ L(axV) ≫ erO⁻¹=ax and cy ≫ L(ayV) ≫ eaFV(G)⁻¹=ay. No scalar action or distributivity law is asserted.

proof.text: Construct ring addition on categorical products sectionwise as the sum of the two projections. The restriction ring homomorphisms preserve sums, so this is a sheaf morphism. Apply the supplied ring hom-equivalence equation to the identity of Lr(O) to express the forgotten ring adjunction unit as the set unit followed by direct image of er.inv. Naturality of the set unit and the product-comparison projection identities identify the two projections of the adjunct of prodComparison followed by prod.map(er.inv,er.inv). Injectivity of the set hom-equivalence reduces the addition transport equation to preservation of sums by the ring adjunction unit, checked on each section.

Apply the operation compatibility theorem for the supplied abelian comparison ea and its hom-equivalence hypothesis to the underlying abelian sheaf of G. Retain its two addition morphisms, section formulas, and product-comparison transport equation.

Precompose each categorical addition with the inverse of the canonical product-to-tensor isomorphism. The conePointUniqueUpToIso inverse projection identities give exactly the sectionwise sums on pairs. In both transport equations, combine the consecutive functor images of the product-to-tensor isomorphism and its inverse, cancel the inverse product comparison with the product comparison, combine the two product maps, and cancel er or ea. This gives the required tensor equations.
